facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of progressively worsening morning headaches
associated with nausea and vomiting
which did not fully resolve with analgesics
numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities
blurred or double vision, vertigo, and a clumsy gait
both vertical and horizontal nystagmus
gait ataxia
a mildly hypodense, 30 × 40 × 40 mm mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region of the posterior fossa
without contrast enhancement or calcifications
with surrounding brain edema and obstructive hydrocephalus
a well-demarcated, relatively homogeneous mass filling the fourth ventricle
causing effacement of the fourth-ventricle outlets, cerebellar compression, and tonsillar herniation

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a mass lesion in the fourth ventricle and obstructive hydrocephalus, are consistent with a medulloblastoma.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a well-demarcated mass filling the fourth ventricle, are consistent with an ependymoma.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a mass lesion in the fourth ventricle and cerebellar compression, are consistent with a cerebellar astrocytoma.
The patient's symptoms, including numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities, are consistent with a brainstem glioma.
The patient's symptoms, including blurred or double vision and vertigo, are consistent with an acoustic neuroma.
The patient's symptoms, including numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities, are consistent with multiple sclerosis.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including cerebellar compression and tonsillar herniation, are consistent with a Chiari malformation.
The patient's symptoms, including numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities, are consistent with cerebral vasculitis.
